cards.explanation: The answer is finished stones for the house of God. David appointed stonecutters from the foreigners in the land of Israel to prepare them. So the stones got shaped before anyone started stacking them. That's the kind of work nobody claps for. I can respect a man who gets the dough ready before the oven is even hot.

The answer is False. The text says David provided a large quantity of iron, together with more bronze than could be weighed. That's no little bit, friends. My kitchen scale would take one look at that pile and ask for a transfer.

The answer is counted. The text says the Sidonians and Tyrians brought David more cedar logs than could be counted. That's a pile past counting, friends. I lose count on a long day of cookie batches, and mine only go up to about forty.

The answer is young and inexperienced. David says, "My son Solomon is young and inexperienced…" Solomon is David's son, and David looks at the size of the job and says he must make preparations. I think that's a dad who knows his son has a long road ahead and wants to make it a little easier.

The answer is True, friends. David says the house to be built for the LORD must be "…exceedingly magnificent" and famous and glorious throughout all lands. Then he adds, "Therefore I must make preparations for it."

The answer is that he has shed so much blood. The LORD told David, "You have shed much blood and waged great wars." He added that David was not to build the house because he had shed so much blood on the ground before Him. It's a hard word to hear, friends, and I think it hurt, even though David had it in his heart to build.

The answer is rest, friends. The LORD said the son would be "…a man of rest." The LORD would give him rest from all his enemies on every side. After a king with great wars behind him, a son of rest is quite the change.

The answer is peace and quiet. God said, "…I will grant to Israel peace and quiet during his reign." That's a promise worth hearing, friends. David had waged great wars (1 Chronicles 22:8), so I bet peace and quiet sounded GOOD.
The answer is False, friends. God said, "…I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever." That doesn't stop when Solomon does. It's a promise much bigger than one man's years.

The answer is insight and understanding. David tells Solomon, "Above all, may the LORD give you insight and understanding when He puts you in command over Israel…" Solomon, David's son, has a big job coming, friends. David puts insight and understanding above all.

The answer is law, friends. David wants Solomon to have insight and understanding "…so that you may keep the Law of the LORD your God." Understanding is for the keeping. Knowing is good, but David wants Solomon doing it too.

The answer is be strong and courageous. David tells Solomon, "Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged." Solomon, David's son, is young and facing a very big job, friends. I think a dad saying that is hoping his boy hears it loud and clear.
The answer is False, friends. David says, "…I have taken great pains to provide for the house of the LORD…" That pile of gold, silver, bronze and iron wasn't gathered easily.

The answer is beyond number. David says the craftsmen in gold and silver, bronze and iron are "beyond number." He also tells Solomon, "You also have many workers…" (1 Chronicles 22:15). Solomon, David's son, isn't short on skilled hands, friends.

The answer is True, friends. David tells the leaders of Israel, "…the land has been subdued before the LORD and His people." He also says the LORD has granted them rest on every side. He's pointing to what has already happened, and now it's time to build.

The answer is the ark of the covenant, friends. David wants them to bring "…the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy articles of God into the temple that will be built for the Name of the LORD." The temple is built for the ark and the holy articles. David is looking all the way to the finished house.
